posts.name: Akshansh
posts.cooked:
Hi,

I wanted to ask whether I can use only PowerShell (with or without running as Administrator) for the System Commands course practice and BPT submissions.

I already have WSL installed because I was previously using Ubuntu 22.04 LTS from the Microsoft Store. As far as I understand, the Microsoft Store version of Ubuntu requires WSL, so I had enabled and installed WSL at that time.

Could you please clarify:

  1. Can I use my previously installed Ubuntu 22.04 LTS through WSL for this course?

  2. Is using PowerShell alone sufficient to complete all course related tasks?

  3. In one of the videos, it was suggested to install a full virtual machine (like VirtualBox) and then install Ubuntu using the official ISO file. Is this setup really required?

  4. If all course activities are CLI-based, can everything be completed using WSL instead of setting up Oracle VirtualBox with Ubuntu?

I recently had college exams, so I was not able to go through all the videos carefully. Please guide me on the correct setup and suggest any specific videos that would help me understand the required environment better.

Thank you.

posts.name: Ishan Shishodiya
posts.cooked:
Do not practice the commands covered in the course in PowerShell. Apart from a few similarly named commands like cd, ls, etc. PowerShell doesn’t have the same available commands as Bash.

You can use WSL to practice locally or the course VM (which requires minimal efforts to setup).

posts.name: Akshansh
posts.cooked: @22f2001554 Can you pls clear the difference between the course vm and WSL? Isn’t course vm just a login to Ubuntu(terminal) to access the files for the course? Or is course vm the VirtualBox setup, which gives the Ubuntu full interface?

posts.name: Ishan Shishodiya
posts.cooked: The course VM is a seperate server which is running Ubuntu while WSL is a compatibility layer between Windows and Linux on your own computer. You can use both for practice, but all your BPTs will be conducted on the course VM.
